subject: axolotl
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.

spec.name: Chibi Axolotl
spec.description: A chubby chibi axolotl with a huge round head, wide smile, bead eyes and three frilly pink gill fronds on each side, standing on four stubby webbed feet with a finned tail.
spec.layout: Chibi proportions: the head is almost as big as the whole torso, a wide flat-topped rounded dome (about 0.30 wide, 0.25 tall, 0.24 long) at the front (+Z) with a short blunt snout. The body behind it is a short chubby bean (z -0.14 to 0.10) with its belly resting on the floor. A tapering, vertically flattened tail with a fin runs back to z = -0.40. Four stubby legs splay out to the sides with tiny finger-like digits (4 on the hands, 5 on the feet) lying flat on the floor. Three feathery gill fronds per side sprout from the back sides of the head and fan up, out and slightly back, and they are the colour hero: hot pink stalks, lighter pink filaments and pale tips. The face is simple and cute: two small glossy black bead eyes with white highlights set wide and high on the front of the head, a wide upturned smile line on a separate lower jaw, two tiny nostril dots, and blush cheeks. The body is pale pink with a cream belly, soft darker pink freckles and a fin ridge along the back. Everything is made of blocky, faceted primitives (low segment counts, 6-10 sides), with small separate parts for the details and each piece in one flat colour. Hands and feet are chunky for their size. Left is +X, right is -X.

parts.builds: The big chibi head and the whole face. A wide, flat-topped rounded skull (loft or squashed sphere with about 10 segments) in skin, with a lighter skinLight top-of-head cap and a short blunt snout. A neck collar blends it into the body. Eyes: dark eye beads (r about 0.018) at the eyeL/eyeR mounts, each with an eyeRing ring behind it and one or two white eyeShine dots, plus a tiny skinShadow brow lid above each. A separate lower jaw on the 'jaw' joint (rounded wedge in skin with a belly-coloured chin), and an upper jaw lip. A mouthInside dark pink mouth cavity with a small tongue between the jaws. A wide upturned smile drawn as a thin mouthLine sweep along the jaw seam that curls up at each corner. Two tiny nostril dots on top of the snout. Cheek blush discs (cheekBlush) on the sides of the face below and behind the eyes. A few freckle dots on top of the head. Small skinShadow ridges where the gill roots leave the head (flush root bumps at the gillRoot mounts, skin colour, no gill geometry). Riding joints head and jaw.
parts.attaches: Neck seam at neckSeam meets the body's front. The gill roots at gillRootL1..3 and gillRootR1..3 are where the gills part begins; the head only has the little skin bumps there.

parts.builds: Six frilly external gills, three per side, the hero feature. Each gill is a stalk (tapered sweep along a short curve, gillStalk at the root fading to gillDark underneath) from its gillRoot mount: L1 upper reaches about (0.20, 0.28, 0.07), L2 middle about (0.25, 0.17, 0.07), L3 lower about (0.22, 0.07, 0.07), mirrored for the right side with a mirrored x. Along each stalk, on both its sides and slightly backward, grow 8-10 feathery filaments: slim tapered spikes or thin sweeps 0.03-0.06 long, longest in the middle and shorter at the tip, fanned out alternately front and back. Filaments are gillFrond with gillTip on their last segment (small tip beads or a separate tip colour part), so the whole fan reads as a bushy pink feather in a root-to-tip palette of gillStalk, gillFrond, gillTip. Each gill hangs on its own joint (gillL1 etc.), with filaments on the same bone as their stalk. Add a small round gillDark base knob where each stalk meets the head.
parts.attaches: Stalks start at the gillRootL1..3/gillRootR1..3 mounts on the sides of the head and are parented to the head joint. Nothing may cover the face or protrude forward of z = 0.17.

parts.builds: The chubby torso: a short fat bean-shaped loft from the neckSeam to the tailRoot (z 0.10 to -0.14), about 0.2 wide and 0.18 tall, belly flattened to rest on the floor, in skin with a belly-coloured underside strip (sectors or a separate belly band) and skinLight shading on the top. Soft freckle spots scattered on the back and flanks (freckle and skinShadow, small flat discs seated on the surface, 15-25 of them). A dorsal fin ridge along the midline of the back from backRidgeStart to the tail root: a thin extruded or membrane fin (fin colour with a finEdge rim and a few finRay lines), rising up to y 0.23. A row of 4-5 faint vertical flank grooves (skinShadow thin sweeps) behind the shoulders, like an axolotl's costal grooves. A small vent bump on the underside near the tail root. Riding joints hips and spine1.
parts.attaches: Front end meets the head at neckSeam; rear end meets the tail at tailRoot. Shoulder and hip sockets at shoulderL/R and hipL/R are covered by limb roots that the limbs part builds, so the torso sides are plain there.

parts.builds: The tapered tail from tailRoot to tailTip: a skin sweep (taller than wide, like a paddle, radius about 0.075 tall and 0.045 wide at the root down to a rounded tip of 0.02), in skin on top fading to belly colour below. A continuous tail fin: a dorsal fin membrane continuing the body's ridge to the tip and a ventral fin below, in fin colour with a finEdge rim line and finRay stripes seated on it, with a gently scalloped edge and a rounded paddle tip. Freckle spots on the tail sides, getting sparser toward the tip. Four joints tail1..tail4, with skin and fin skinned to them.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailRoot, meeting the body's rear; the fin ridge continues straight on from the body's dorsal fin at y about 0.19 near z = -0.12.

parts.builds: Four stubby splayed legs with chunky hands and feet. Each leg is a short two-segment skin sweep (upper arm/thigh then forearm/shin) ending flat on the floor, thick for its length (radius about 0.028 tapering to 0.02), with a round skin shoulder/hip bulb that covers the socket on the body. Front hands lie at handL/handR with 4 thick, short digits (tapered rods or capsules, toe colour with toeTip tips) fanned forward, with a flat round palm pad; back feet at footL/footR have 5 digits and a slightly larger flat sole, turned slightly outward. Digits sit on the elbow/knee bones. Little skinShadow wrist/ankle creases and a few freckles on the upper limbs. Everything is rounded and chubby, not thin. Joints shoulderL/R, elbowL/R, hipL/R, kneeL/R.
parts.attaches: Shoulder sockets at shoulderL/R on the body sides, hip sockets at hipL/R. Hands and feet rest on y = 0 outside the body and head silhouette (x beyond 0.15 at the front).

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out proportions for a chibi axolotl with frilly pink gills—planning a big round head, chubby short body, and curved tail, aiming for roughly a 0.5 meter overall length.

I'm working out the detailed shapes: stubby legs with tiny digits, three feathery gill stalks per side, a wide smiling mouth with small spaced eyes, and pale pink cheeks, then mapping these onto approximate box coordinates for head, body, and tail. I'm also laying out the skeleton joints—hips as root, a spine joint, and a head joint—to position everything correctly in 3D space.

Now I'm placing the jaw joint under the head, then setting up the gill joints along the back of the head with directions fanning up-out, out, and out-down for the upper, middle, and lower gills. I'm also chaining the tail joints backward from the hips with a tail direction, and starting the shoulder joint for the front leg with an outward-downward direction.

I'll keep the limb chains simple: shoulderL/elbowL for the arm and hipL/kneeL for the leg, skipping separate digit joints for simplicity. Now I'm defining the first part, the head, listing its sub-features (skull, cheeks, eyes, mouth, jaw, nostrils, snout, freckles, brow, crest) with its bounding box and floor contact, then moving to the gills part with its own bounding box.

For the body I'm including the torso, belly, markings, dorsal fin, and cloaca with hip and spine joints, resting on the floor. Then for the tail I'm setting up joints tail1-4, a shrinking fin sweep with gradient color and spots, and weighing whether the tail tip should lift off the floor or stay grounded.

Legs come next: four limbs with hands and digits, bone joints, positioned with floor contact true. I'm allocating budgets across parts—roughly 200 for head, 220 gills, 120 body, 110 tail, 160 limbs, totaling 810—and settling on a leucistic axolotl palette with pale pink skin, lighter highlights, and vivid pink-red gills.

Now I'm filling out the rest of the color palette—gill stalks, fronds, tips, eyes, mouth, fins, nails, spots—and defining the joint mounts connecting head, neck, and jaw at specific coordinates.

I'm placing the gill roots, shoulder, hip, and tail mounts, along with the body-head seam, then sketching out the body's overall dimensions and center position.

I'm sizing the body box, deciding the dorsal fin ridge runs from the body into the tail, and raising the body's upper bound to accommodate it. Then I'm defining the head's dimensions, center position, and rough eye placement on top.

Now I'm placing the eyes dorsolaterally near the front as big black beads with highlights, adding a wide mouth line and cheek blush for the chibi style, then working out gill placement -- roots on the head's back sides sweeping outward, upward, and backward, trying to set a bounding box for the gills that doesn't overlap awkwardly with the body.

Overall I'm settling on a total length from tail to head of about 0.71, giving an overall size of roughly 0.54 by 0.31 by 0.71. For the limbs, I'm defining front leg joints from shoulder to elbow to a stubby four-digit hand fanning forward, and rear legs from hip to knee to a five-digit foot pointing forward, then checking that the limb bounding box doesn't clash with the head's dimensions.

I'm adjusting the front hand positions so they sit in front of the head rather than overlapping it, nudging the x and z coordinates until the digit tips clear the head's surface at each height. With that resolved, I'm now laying out the joint hierarchy -- spine chain with hips as root, spine1 above it, and the head attached further up, each with parent relationships and direction vectors defined.

I'm also working through the jaw joint placement, reasoning about where the hinge should sit relative to the mouth corners so the jaw opens naturally from inside the head. Then I'm defining the tail chain as a sequence of segments extending backward from the hips, tapering in radius from base to tip and shaped with a slight dorsal/ventral fin so the lowest points rest against the floor in the default pose.

Now I'm laying out the gill joints branching off the head, mirrored left and right, each with its own direction vector and tapering root-to-tip positions to form a fan-like frond structure.
